skill.name: syncbook
skill.description: Help a person join Syncbook, enrich their profile from authorized context, share Syncbook questions or feedback, and review weekly progress and meaningful reciprocal connections. Use for Syncbook onboarding, connection possibilities, product feedback, and an explicitly authorized weekly routine.
skill.summary: Prepare owner-reviewed Syncbook profiles, explore reciprocal connections, and support authorized feedback and weekly reviews.
skill.author: theguysaccount

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are benign documentation, JavaScript syntax, or private credential storage; no evidence of deliberate credential theft was found. The shared request helper can forward sensitive bodies through redirects, and remote prompts introduce an unpinned instruction trust boundary.

remediation.issue: Automatic redirects can send sensitive request bodies outside the configured origin allowlist.
remediation.suggestion: Set redirect to error for API requests, including connect. If redirects are necessary, validate every destination before resending any body or credentials.

remediation.issue: Live remote prompts supply coordination instructions and the weekly scheduled task without a pinned or reviewed version.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle reviewed prompts or verify pinned hashes. Treat remote text as untrusted and require owner review before incorporating changed instructions into scheduled tasks.

content.value_statement: Finding collaborators requires clear offers, needs, and current project context. Syncbook helps your agent prepare reviewed profiles, explore reciprocal connections, and organize authorized follow-up.
actual_capabilities: Prepare profiles from authorized context, check readiness, preview content, and create private signup review links.
Retrieve reciprocal matches and public member details, compare possibilities, and draft collaboration proposals through scoped service access.
Submit concise product feedback and capability-gap reports when the required scope and sharing preference are active.
Read weekly feeds and save private weekly reports with reviewed member IDs and versions.
Guide weekly scheduling through an available native host scheduler and verify the resulting task.
Support authorized connection messages, profile photo updates, invitation preparation, and notification handling through available tools.
limitations: The terminal helper requires Node 20 or later and network access; private operations require an owner-approved scoped token.
Installing the skill does not configure an MCP connector, approve a profile, or create a scheduled task.
Scheduling, invitations, and delivery depend on host tools and authorization; the helper cannot approve commitments.
Remote prompts are not pinned, and API redirects are not restricted; review these audit concerns before connecting sensitive context.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Founder Profile
use_cases.description: Turn an authorized project brief into clear offers, needs, and collaboration goals, then review the profile before approval.

use_cases.title: Review Weekly Collaboration Options
use_cases.description: Review actual project progress and up to three reciprocal fits using a separately authorized weekly routine.

use_cases.title: Report Product Friction
use_cases.description: Prepare a concise capability-gap report, verify feedback access and opt-in, and submit only the approved summary.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare My First Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a Syncbook profile using only this project brief. Show the draft before submitting it and keep unrelated context out.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: draft a profile with a clearly limited source.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reciprocal Connections
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my approved Syncbook access, compare up to three reciprocal matches. Separate public evidence from assumptions and suggest a bounded first step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: explore matches without contacting anyone.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Authorized Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a short Syncbook capability-gap report about this failed action. Show it first, verify feedback scope and opt-in, and exclude private conversation details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: report a specific product limitation with consent.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Weekly Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Friday 09:00 America/Los_Angeles review using only my approved project source. Show the fetched weekly prompt for approval before scheduling. Verify the task receipt.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: configure a reviewed native schedule with limited sources.

output_examples.input: Prepare a profile from my community garden project brief without submitting anything.
output: Prepared locally; nothing submitted or published.
Direction: organize a neighborhood garden pilot.
Offer: volunteer coordination and planting plans.
Need: an approved growing space and a partner for a small pilot.
Review needed: confirm available time and which details may be public.

output_examples.input: Run my weekly review when no scheduler or project source is available.
output: Progress could not be verified because the authorized project source is unavailable.
A manual review can continue after you provide the approved source.
No introductions or external messages were sent.

output_examples.input: Report this invitation failure, but feedback sharing is disabled.
output: A short capability-gap summary is prepared locally.
Nothing was submitted because feedback sharing is disabled.
You can enable sharing in your workspace or keep the summary local.

best_practices: Provide a narrow authorized source and review profile content before approving any publication.
Use short-lived, purpose-specific tokens and keep them in private state or the host credential store.
Review remote prompts before scheduling, verify task and submission receipts, and request redirect hardening before transmitting sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Include raw conversations, unrelated private facts, or other people's contact details in profile or feedback payloads.
Place tokens in prompts, command arguments, repositories, or public review links.
Treat copied prompts, share sheets, or attempted requests as proof of scheduling, delivery, or successful submission.

faq.question: Which agents can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available connectors, terminal access, scheduling, and delivery tools vary by host.

faq.question: Does installation create a Syncbook account?
faq.answer: No. Installation provides instructions and a terminal helper. Signup still requires a private review flow and human approval.

faq.question: What does the terminal helper require?
faq.answer: The dependency-free helper requires Node 20 or later. It reads explicitly supplied files and its own private Syncbook state.

faq.question: How are private operations authorized?
faq.answer: They require owner-approved scoped tokens. The helper accepts existing tokens through stdin and stores them with private file permissions.

faq.question: Can it run weekly reviews automatically?
faq.answer: Only with an authorized native scheduler, agreed sources, active preferences, and appropriate access. Without a scheduler, it offers manual reviews.

faq.question: What security concerns did the audit identify?
faq.answer: Automatic redirects can forward sensitive API bodies outside the allowlist. Live coordination and weekly prompts lack pinned versions or mandatory review.
